# Concurrent replies — one live reply per CHAT, not per tab

*Status: design. Nothing here is built. Written 2026-08-16 against `ai.js` at
0.129.0 and `api` at `47d3a6e`.*

Today a reply streaming in one chat locks the composer in **every** chat, and
the landing says *"Wait for the current reply to finish"*. The intended
invariant — written down in PRD 7.5 and still unbuilt — is **one live reply
per chat**, enforced by the server. What shipped is **one live reply per
browser tab**, enforced by the client. This document is the difference
between those two sentences, and the order in which to close it.

## 1. The constraint is a single boolean and a single slot

Both are module-global in `ai.js` and neither is keyed by chat:

```js
sending: false,   // ai.js:1281 — a reply is streaming
stream:  null,    // ai.js:1291 — "keyed by its chat" (the comment is wrong)
```

`S.stream` holds one stream object carrying a `chatId` field. It is written
unconditionally in `streamReply` and `resumeReply`; a second write silently
evicts the first. Every composer reader shares one predicate:

```js
function turnInFlight() {                    // ai.js:2922
  return !!(S.sending || (S.stream && !S.stream.done) || S.stopping[S.chatId]);
}
```

The first two terms take no `chatId`, so this is true on **every** screen the
moment any reply anywhere is streaming. That is the whole lock. `S.stopping`,
`S.queue`, `S.queueHeld` and `S.drafts` are *already* per-chat — `sending` and
`stream` are the only two that are not.

**There is no server guard.** `StreamRepliesView.create` validates the chat,
enforces the monthly money quota, closes an orphaned pause *for that one
chat*, writes the reply row and spawns. Nothing anywhere asks whether another
reply is already generating — not for this chat, not for this user, not for
this business. `_spawn` is a bare daemon thread with no pool, no semaphore and
no counter. Two concurrent `curl` POSTs to two chats both succeed today.

## 2. Why it exists — an artifact, not a decision

Four candidate reasons were on the table. Three are ruled out by the code:

- **Not money.** `enforce_ai_quota` is a monthly, per-business *money* check.
  It counts no live replies.
- **Not the queue's one-at-a-time rule.** That rule is real, but it is about
  draining one queued prompt per turn *within* a chat, so there is always a
  moment to intervene. `S.queue` is keyed by chat and `drainQueue` bails on a
  chat that is not on screen. It says nothing about a second chat.
- **Not a shared connection.** Each reply opens its own `fetch` with its own
  reader. There is no multiplexed socket.

What it actually is: `streamReply`, `paintStream`, `attachStreamTail` and
`streamingHere` all render through the module-level `messagesEl` and compare
against the module-level `S.chatId`. `postAndStream` appends the user bubble
straight into `messagesEl`, so a turn started from a different chat would push
its message into the *visible* pane. One slot was the shape that made that
impossible. Phase 5's author documented exactly this in
`ai-prompt-queue.md:648`, and phase 5 made the lock *visible* rather than
creating it — before that the press was silently swallowed.

The **landing** has one additional and genuinely separate reason: `/new` has
no chat id, so it cannot queue, and phase 5 chose locked-and-says-so over
silently-eaten. That argument is about the queue's fallback, and it evaporates
the moment `/new` is allowed to start its own turn — because then there is
nothing to queue.

## 3. The ordering is INVERTED from 5.2 and 5.4, deliberately

Phases 5.2 and 5.4 shipped the UI half first, because the UI is what
established the contract the API then implemented. **Do not do that here.**

Today the client's global lock is silently performing a data-integrity job the
server was supposed to do. It is the only thing preventing two `generating`
replies in one chat — the state `regenerate`'s own comment calls "the state
that wedges the client", and `close_orphaned_pause`'s docstring calls
pathological. Relaxing the client first opens that hole for however long the
two halves are apart, and `ai.js` ships from the CDN to servers of every age,
so **assume the new client reaches users before the new server does.**

So: **stage 5 first.** It is safe on its own, it is strictly more restrictive
than today, and it closes the hole independently of any client work.

## 4. Stages

**S5 — [api] The guard PRD 7.5 specifies.** In `StreamRepliesView.create`,
after `close_orphaned_pause` and *before* the `Message.objects.create`, refuse
with 409 when the chat already has a message in `Message.LIVE_STATES`
(`GENERATING, AWAITING_INPUT` — so a chat paused on a question or an approval
also refuses, exactly as the composer does today). A **conditional write, not
check-then-act**, in the discipline `close_orphaned_pause` already documents,
so it cannot race a second POST. Give it a stable machine-readable `code`
beside the queue's five and StopView's three, because `ai.js` branches on the
code. Safe to ship alone.

**S1 — [sdk] Make the registry plural.** Pure refactor, no behaviour change.
`S.stream` → `S.streams = {}` keyed by chatId; `S.sending` → `S.sendingIn =
{}`. One accessor `liveStream(chatId)` returning the entry when it exists and
is not `done`. ~29 lines mention `S.stream` and 19 mention `S.sending`; most
already have a chatId in scope (`st.chatId` or `S.chatId`). Frees become
`if (S.streams[st.chatId] === st) delete …`. **Ship as a standalone commit
with no behaviour change**, so a bisect can isolate it: the existing suite,
including the test that pins today's landing lock, is the check that nothing
moved.

**S2 — [sdk] Make the predicate take a chat.** The change actually asked for:

```js
function turnInFlight(chatId) {
  chatId = chatId || S.chatId;
  return !!(S.sendingIn[chatId] || liveStream(chatId) || S.stopping[chatId]);
}
```

Callers pass their own chat. `queueState` already *has* a `chatId` argument
and was wrongly reading the global — that is a live bug this fixes in passing.
Within one chat everything behaves as today: queue mid-reply, refuse into a
pause.

**S3 — [sdk] The landing's own turn.** `send()` sets `S.sending = true` before
the chat-creation POST resolves, and in a plural world there is no id to key
on yet. Add `S.creatingChat`, scoped to `/new` only, cleared in both the
`.then` and the `.catch`. This is a *genuine* lock — two presses on `/new` a
second apart must not create two chats — and it is the correct remaining home
for the "Wait for the current reply to finish" string, or replace it with
"Starting a new chat…". Either way the key stays in all eight catalogues or
the translation test fails. The existing test asserting the old behaviour must
be rewritten, and a new one added for the double-`/new` press.

**S4 — [sdk] Rendering and Stop.** `attachStreamTail`, `paintStream`,
`streamingHere` and `loadConversation`'s `liveHere` key off
`liveStream(S.chatId)`. `stopTarget` likewise, so Stop on chat B addresses
chat B. Add a running indicator per chat in the sidebar — the entire point of
this change is that a reply now runs somewhere nobody is looking. Extend the
`beforeunload` guard to count live streams, not just queued prompts.

**S6 — [api] The bill, before this is advertised.** (a) `enforce_ai_quota` is
read-then-spend with no reservation, so N concurrent turns each read the same
under-limit total: a workspace can overshoot by up to N−1 turns. The client
lock currently hides this; S2 removes the hiding. Either reserve-then-settle,
or accept and *document* a bounded overshoot. (b) Each live reply costs two
threads and two DB connections — the generation thread and the request thread
running `tail_message`'s 0.12s poll — for up to fifteen minutes on a paused
reply, on a single-process `runserver`. Going from 1 to N per user multiplies
both linearly. Raise the poll interval for long-idle tails, or land the real
WSGI worker config sitting in the same PRD bullet.

## 5. What gets worse, honestly

- **The queue in a background chat does not drain.** It is per-chat already,
  but auto-drain fires only from `commitStream` for the chat on screen.
  `ai-prompt-queue.md:653` already states this; today it is rare because you
  can only have one live chat, and concurrency makes it the common case. The
  strip's "Sending when this reply finishes" becomes a promise about a chat
  nobody is looking at.
- **Cross-tab is unchanged in kind, multiplied in degree.** There is no
  cross-tab arbiter today and this adds none. It multiplies the number of
  simultaneously-unreconciled replies per user.
- **A stray reload destroys N replies instead of one**, none of them on
  screen.
- **The per-tree budget from 6.2 is NOT affected.** Two top-level chats are
  two trees with two budgets; concurrency cannot let one tree spend another's.
  Stated explicitly because it is the first thing that looks at risk.

## 6. The shortest honest path

S5, then S1+S2. That gives one live reply per chat, server-enforced, with the
client no longer speaking for every chat at once. S3 and S4 make it feel
finished; S6 is what has to be true before it is something users are told
about.
